title: FocusTrap
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.ui.window.Dialog, MonarchDialog, MonarchBottomSheet, androidx.compose.ui.window.Popup with PopupProperties(focusable = true)
summary: Keeping focus inside a modal surface is done by the platform's modal windows: Dialog, MonarchDialog, MonarchBottomSheet and a focusable Popup each open a window that holds TalkBack and keyboard focus. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For any surface that must be finished or dismissed before the rest of the screen can be used: a confirmation, a form in a dialog, a sheet of options.
whenNotToUse: For content that may be used alongside the screen, such as a side panel or a non-modal tooltip, use a non-modal container and let focus move freely.
api: @Composable fun Dialog(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, properties: DialogProperties = DialogProperties(), content: @Composable () -> Unit)

@Composable fun MonarchDialog(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, title: String?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, dismissible: Boolean = true, dismissOnClickOutside: Boolean = dismissible, paneTitle: String? = null, actions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null, content: (@Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchBottomSheet(onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, description: String? = null, dismissible: Boolean = true, showHandle: Boolean = true, fullyExpanded: Boolean = true, fullWidthContent: Boolean = false, content: @Composable MonarchBottomSheetScope.() -> Unit)

@Composable fun Popup(alignment: Alignment = Alignment.TopStart, offset: IntOffset = IntOffset(0, 0), onDismissRequest: (() -> Unit)? = null, properties: PopupProperties = PopupProperties(), content: @Composable () -> Unit)

states.name: shown
states.description: The modal window holds focus. TalkBack and the keyboard cannot reach the screen behind it.

states.name: dismissed
states.description: Back, a tap on the scrim or a button calls onDismissRequest; the app removes the window and focus returns to the screen.

appearance: No appearance of its own: dialogs and sheets take the Monarch colors through MonarchTheme's Material 3 mapping, in light, dark and high contrast.
platformNotes: The web needs a FocusTrap component and hook because a browser lets Tab leave a dialog. On Android a Dialog, MonarchBottomSheet or focusable Popup is a separate window, so TalkBack and the keyboard stay inside it. The web's initialFocus is a FocusRequester with requestFocus() in a LaunchedEffect inside the window; returnFocus is the system's; onEscape is onDismissRequest, which Back and Escape trigger. iOS uses sheet and fullScreenCover in the same way.
accessibility: System behavior: a dialog or modal sheet is a separate window; TalkBack and keyboard focus stay inside it until it is dismissed.
System behavior: Back, and Escape on a hardware keyboard, call onDismissRequest unless the properties turn that off.
A Popup only takes focus with PopupProperties(focusable = true); a non-focusable popup does not confine focus.
Give a dialog a title so TalkBack announces it when it opens.
edgeCases: MonarchDialog(dismissible = false), or DialogProperties(dismissOnBackPress = false) on a Dialog, keeps a dialog with unsaved changes open; keep a visible button that dismisses it.
A custom overlay drawn inside the screen (a Box over the content) does not confine focus; use Dialog or Popup instead.
The catalogue page opens the dialog and the sheet only on a tap; the compiled example shows the dialog closed until a button is pressed.
